title: Worker-owned durable Rate Browse and Print merge execution with timeout and reaper fences

acceptanceCriteria.description: Rate Browse provider fan-out is claimed and executed by a pg-boss worker from durable serializable input; the API-local queueMicrotask scheduler is removed.
One active request key and generation-conditional writes prevent simultaneous same-fingerprint work and stale Rate Browse or PDF workers from publishing over a successor.
Print merge runs in the dedicated worker from persisted inputs, publishes mandatory generation-fenced chunks before done, releases completed base64 bytes, and resumes stored chunks after restart.
Deadline cancellation keeps durable or lane ownership until admitted work settles, and the reaper uses timeout plus grace and never reaps a held live lane.
Startup and periodic recovery requeue queued or stale Rate Browse and Print merge generations without duplicating PS-423 provider receipt/postage policy.
The focused failure/restart suite, all mandatory source-of-truth guards, strict TypeScript checks, and production frontend build pass at the reviewed implementation SHA.
Verification created no live label, postage, provider notification, marketplace confirmation, or production orders/shipments mutation, and shipped/cancelled protections were not weakened.

canonicalOwners: src/services/rate-browse-worker.ts plus rate_browse_jobs durable claim/generation state
src/services/print-queue-worker.ts plus print_queue_merge_jobs durable claim/generation state

oldOwners.path: src/services/print-queue.ts startPrintJob direct API runMergeJob invocation
fixed sync reaper age independent of configured handler timeout

wrappers.delegatesTo: startRateBrowseWorkflow durable intent persistence and worker enqueue
durable merge store, dedicated worker claim, and chunk artifact owner

sotBypass.details: Routes only persist/enqueue intent and return/read DTOs. Provider fan-out, merge execution, recovery, cancellation acknowledgement, terminal state, and artifact publication remain in named durable backend owners.

evidence.proves: A migrated PostgreSQL-compatible database retains worker input and artifacts, exposes stale jobs for restart recovery, increments a new generation, and preserves already-written chunks across the simulated restart boundary.
Concurrent duplicate active requests and overlapping fresh claims are rejected; stale snapshot writes, stale artifact overwrites, and stale new artifact inserts have zero durable effect.

A non-cooperative attempt exceeds its deadline but the cancellation remains unacknowledged and the claim remains held until the original work settles; only then is acknowledgement recorded and recovery allowed.

Migration 0067 applies to legacy-shaped sidecar tables, reconciles duplicate active job metadata, installs the unique/fence indexes and columns, and still accepts previous-application inserts that omit every new column.
API detached execution is absent, worker enqueue/claim/recovery wiring is present, chunk bytes are released from memory, and timeout-derived reaper ownership is pinned against regression.
The static ownership guard and executable migrated-database/failure-injection proof run as one focused PS-428 command.
All 43 mandatory source-of-truth and lifecycle guards pass with PS-428 wired into both the pack and its guard-of-guard.
Backend and frontend strict TypeScript checks pass.
The production frontend bundle builds successfully with 2,989 modules transformed.

The reviewed implementation changes durable job/artifact orchestration and offline proof only. Migration 0067 contains no orders/shipments mutation, and no test invokes a live provider, buys postage, or notifies a marketplace.
After applying migration 0067, legacy application inserts that omit all PS-428 columns still succeed; operational code rollback can safely leave the additive sidecars and indexes in place.

migrations.rollbackPlan: Revert the application commit while leaving additive job/artifact columns and indexes in place. The integration proof confirms the previous application can still insert/read legacy-shaped rows. The one-time duplicate-active reconciliation affects only transient Rate Browse sidecar metadata and is intentionally not reversed.

rollback.strategy: Revert the packet commit and implementation commit. Leave migration 0067's additive columns and indexes in place so in-flight sidecar/artifact history remains readable; the previous application ignores the new fields and its legacy inserts are verified against the migrated fixture.

liveVerification.reason: The required durable-job proof is executable against a PostgreSQL-compatible migrated fixture with injected timeout/crash/concurrency failures. No live provider, label purchase, postage, marketplace notification, or production orders/shipments mutation is required for closure; deployment health is checked separately after push.
